flow.costPlain: What Home Depot paid suppliers for the merchandise it sold, plus the cost of getting it into stores.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Store payroll, rent, advertising and running the head office — up 3.4%, slower than sales.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of stores, warehouses and equipment over their useful lives — including $182M of amortization tied to acquired companies like SRS.

follow100Note: Two-thirds of every $100 goes straight back out as the cost of the merchandise itself — retail keeps a much thinner slice than software does. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Nine-month free cash flow was $12,817M. Guidance for fiscal 2026: sales +~4.5%, comparable sales +~1.4%, diluted EPS +~1.5%.
oneTimers: Adjusted results exclude $182M of amortization from acquired intangibles (mostly SRS) — on that basis EPS was $3.86 instead of the GAAP $3.72. It is a recurring accounting charge, not a one-off.

No quarterly cash flow: the release's cash-flow statement covers the nine-month period only, so Q3 operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow cannot be stated — the $12,817M free cash flow is a nine-month figure.
Acquisitions are in the comparison: SRS locations (1,320+) are now part of the store base, so part of the year-over-year sales growth reflects businesses that weren't in the base a year ago.
otherDetail: Interest and other, net was a $528M cost: $579M of interest expense on Home Depot's debt, partly offset by $51M of interest and other income.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold through 2,372 Home Depot stores and its website, plus the SRS and GMS professional-supply businesses Home Depot has been buying to win more contractor spending.

takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 2.2% with the average ticket up 3.0% while comparable transactions fell 0.5% — bigger baskets, not more baskets. That's fine while ticket growth holds, but leaves little cushion if big-ticket demand cools.
takeaways.title: Same-store growth is ticket-led, not traffic-led

takeaways.text: Gross margin fell 0.6 points to 32.8% because cost of sales (+6.0%) outran sales (+4.9%); SG&A actually grew slower than sales. Watch whether supplier costs keep outpacing prices, or whether Home Depot passes them through.
takeaways.title: The margin squeeze is in the goods, not the stores

takeaways.text: Updated guidance implies only about 1.5% diluted EPS growth for fiscal 2026 (2.0% adjusted) — the year is about holding margin, not a second-half acceleration. Nine-month free cash flow of $12.8B funds the dividend and the ~$2.2B of net interest with room to spare.
takeaways.title: The full-year bar is modest

verdict: Home Depot grew sales 4.9% with comparable sales up 2.2%, but the growth came from bigger tickets, not more shoppers — transactions fell — and margins slipped as the cost of goods grew faster than sales.
